output.title: Synthetic test data: use it for the gap, not the whole workflow
output.body:
Synthetic test data is useful when it solves a specific testing problem. It is not useful when it becomes the thing you are building.

For an owner-run small business, the decision is usually simple: do you need synthetic data because of privacy or scale, or do you just need to test one repeatable workflow with a small batch of real records and a human approval step?

If the pilot is invoice handling or customer inquiry triage, start there. Use a small real-data subset, clear rules, and keep money decisions under human approval. That keeps the work focused on the workflow, not on the theatre of perfect fake data.

Bareni’s accounts-payable demo shows the mechanics with entirely synthetic data: text-based extraction, arithmetic checks, duplicate blocking, and audit records. But it also has clear limits. The default route uses pre-extracted files, and PDF/scan ingestion plus OCR are not implemented. So it is a useful demo for control logic, not proof that every real invoice pile is covered.

My practical next step: pick one workflow, one approval rule, and one small batch of real records. Then ask whether synthetic data is removing a real blocker, or just delaying the moment you learn what the workflow actually needs.
